abstract: Objective: Gut-brain-axis abnormalities are increasingly implicated in Parkinson disease (PD), but most studies examine individual biological compartments of this axis. We asked whether readily accessible stool and plasma-based biomarker profiles show broad or selective gut abnormalities in PD and whether the profiles associated with PD diagnosis (Trait) are the same as those associated with clinical severity (State). Methods: This cross-sectional study included 211 participants with PD and 204 healthy controls. Twenty-four stool and plasma biomarkers were organized into an overall profile, three parent domains (microbiome/dysbiosis, gut barrier/inflammation, systemic inflammation/immune activation), and eight more focused mechanistic profiles. Rank-based Global Statistical Tests (GSTs) compared PD Trait and State. Results: The overall profile showed no evidence of a PD vs. control difference (GST P=0.607; permutation P=0.521), whereas the domain of microbiome/dysbiosis differed (GST P=0.017; permutation P=0.013). Four of eight focused profiles differed nominally: microbial functional-groups, microbial functional-ratios, epithelial injury/bacterial translocation, and myeloid activation. Across PD clinical severity, overall-profile results differed (GST P=0.053; permutation P=0.037); both categories of microbiome/dysbiosis (GST P=0.023; permutation P=0.016) and microbial alpha-diversity (GST P=0.027; permutation P=0.031) differed. Interpretation: The analyses detected differences associated with PD Trait and State in selected gut-related profiles rather than a detectable overall PD-control difference. Microbiome-related profiles showed the most consistent domain findings across PD Trait and State, but they are sufficiently different to suggest that causation and progression of PD follow distinctly different gut processes. These findings refine the concept of the Parkinson gut and prioritize the microbiome for mechanistic and interventional studies.

summary: Stool and plasma biomarker profiles in 211 Parkinson patients and 204 controls show microbiome/dysbiosis differences tied to PD diagnosis and clinical severity.
title: Selective Gut-Related Biomarker Profiles Define Parkinson Disease Trait and State
